blocks.text: Maritime career
Third Officer — Merchant Navy

blocks.label: Recommended degree
blocks.text: B.Sc. in Nautical Science

A Third Officer is an entry-level licensed deck officer aboard a merchant ship. The role involves safe navigation, bridge watchkeeping, shipboard safety equipment, emergency preparedness, and cargo-related duties as assigned. It is a professional seafaring career that requires approved maritime education, mandatory training, medical fitness, and the appropriate Certificate of Competency.
What does a Third Officer do?

Keeps a navigational watch under the ship's established command structure, assists with passage planning and position monitoring, and helps ensure that navigation follows applicable rules and procedures.
Safety responsibilities

May maintain assigned lifesaving and firefighting equipment, participate in drills, inspect safety equipment, and support emergency preparedness according to the vessel's procedures and the officer's assigned duties.
Where they work
Commercial shipping companies operating container ships, bulk carriers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and other merchant vessels for which the officer holds the required qualifications.

sections.heading: Education and eligibility pathway in India

blocks.text: The Merchant Navy is a regulated profession. Admission to a nautical science degree alone does not automatically qualify someone to serve as a Third Officer.

rows.text: School education
Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics for the usual B.Sc. Nautical Science entry route
Academic eligibility
Commonly at least 60% aggregate in PCM and 50% in English in Class 10 or 12; exact requirements must be checked against current official admission rules
Undergraduate degree
B.Sc. Nautical Science from an appropriately approved maritime institute
Duration
Commonly 3 years of pre-sea academic and practical training for the degree route
Medical fitness
Must meet applicable maritime medical standards, including eyesight and colour-vision requirements
Safety training
Required STCW basic safety training and other applicable courses
Sea service and certification
Required training, qualifying sea service, examinations, and a valid Certificate of Competency (CoC) under the applicable Indian maritime rules

blocks.label: Critical distinction
blocks.text: Completing B.Sc. Nautical Science is not the same as holding a Third Officer licence. The route to appointment depends on current Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) requirements, approved training, qualifying sea service, examinations, and certification.
Before paying admission or placement fees, verify that the institute and programme are approved for the intended pathway and confirm the current eligibility and medical requirements.
Check Class 12 PCM marks, English marks, age limits, medical fitness, eyesight, and colour vision against the current rules for your admission year.
Enrol in an approved B.Sc. Nautical Science programme, commonly a three-year residential course, and complete its academic, simulator, practical, and safety-training requirements.

sections.heading: Join a vessel as a deck cadet

blocks.text: Obtain an eligible sea berth and complete the prescribed onboard training and qualifying sea service. Keep the required training record book and supporting documentation.

sections.heading: Qualify for the relevant Certificate of Competency

blocks.text: Complete the applicable courses, sea-service requirements, assessments, and examinations for the Second Mate (Foreign Going) Certificate of Competency, subject to current rules. The maritime authority publishes the relevant examination and certification requirements.
Directorate General of Shipping

After meeting certification, medical, documentation, and employer requirements, apply for a Third Officer position. Actual appointment depends on a suitable vacancy and the company's selection process.

The official maritime career guidance describes the B.Sc. Nautical Science route as three years of campus training followed by a period of sea service before attempting the relevant competency examination. Verify the current sea-time requirement and examination pathway with the Directorate General of Maritime Administration before making financial or admission decisions.
Directorate General of Shipping
Year 1
Seamanship and maritime foundations

items.text: Study navigation fundamentals, nautical terminology, ship structure, and basic seamanship.
Learn maritime safety, emergency procedures, life-saving equipment, and fire prevention.
Practise chartwork, basic navigation calculations, and nautical mathematics.
Develop discipline, teamwork, communication, and professional English.
Understand life aboard a ship, shipboard hierarchy, and maritime conduct.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: explain basic ship operations and demonstrate foundational seamanship knowledge.
Year 2
Navigation, ship stability, and cargo

items.text: Study coastal and celestial navigation fundamentals, chartwork, and voyage planning.
Learn ship stability, buoyancy, loading principles, and cargo-handling fundamentals.
Understand meteorology, tides, currents, and oceanographic conditions.
Practise bridge communication, collision-avoidance rules, and watchkeeping procedures.
Use bridge simulators and navigation equipment in supervised training.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: solve navigation exercises and explain how officers maintain safe navigation and vessel stability.
Year 3
Advanced navigation and sea-readiness

items.text: Study passage planning, electronic navigation, maritime regulations, and bridge resource management.
Learn cargo operations, shipboard documentation, safety management, and emergency response.
Practise radar and ARPA concepts, ECDIS, and Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) fundamentals as covered by the programme.
Complete the required practical training, assessments, and approved safety courses.
Prepare for onboard training and the transition to a deck-cadet role.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: demonstrate the academic and practical competence required for the next approved stage of training.
After graduation
Sea service and officer certification

items.text: Secure a suitable deck-cadet berth with a shipping company.
Complete prescribed onboard training and sea service.
Maintain the training record book and required certificates.
Complete the applicable competency courses and examinations.
Apply for a Third Officer appointment once the required certification and employer conditions are satisfied.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: meet the applicable licensing and sea-service requirements—not merely complete the degree.

rows.text: Navigation
Chartwork, position fixing, passage planning, route monitoring
Watchkeeping
Bridge procedures, lookout duties, handover, situational awareness
Collision avoidance
COLREGs, radar interpretation, safe speed, risk assessment
Electronic navigation
ECDIS, radar, ARPA, GNSS, and relevant bridge systems
Ship stability
Buoyancy, trim, stability, loading effects, cargo fundamentals
Maritime safety
Fire prevention, lifesaving appliances, emergency response, drills
Communication
Maritime English, bridge communication, reporting, teamwork
Regulations
STCW requirements, SOLAS, MARPOL, and relevant maritime rules
Professional discipline
Fatigue awareness, accurate records, situational awareness, compliance

blocks.text: A Third Officer must be able to follow established procedures, communicate clearly, maintain a proper watch, and escalate concerns promptly. Shipboard decisions can affect the vessel, cargo, crew, and marine environment.
Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS)
Learn electronic chart use, route planning, safety settings, alarms, and cross-checking position information.
Radar and ARPA
Understand target detection, relative motion, collision-risk assessment, and the limitations of radar-derived information.
Position and heading systems
Understand GNSS, gyrocompasses, magnetic compasses, heading sensors, and the need to cross-check information using appropriate independent sources.
Safety and emergency equipment
Learn the purpose, inspection requirements, and operating principles of assigned lifesaving and firefighting equipment.
These systems must be learned through approved instruction and supervised practical training. Familiarity with a simulator or online tutorial does not authorise independent operation aboard a ship.

The exact certificates required depend on the intended vessel, flag, duties, and current regulations. Build a checklist with your approved maritime institute and employer rather than relying on a generic list.

blocks.text: When evaluating a shipping-company sponsorship or cadetship offer, ask:

items.text: Is the company or recruitment arrangement legitimate and verifiable?
Is the berth confirmed, or is placement only a possibility?
Who pays for pre-sea training, travel, examinations, and onboard training?
What is the expected cadet stipend, contract duration, and leave arrangement?
What happens if a sea berth is delayed?
What are the documented steps from deck cadet to the required Certificate of Competency?

blocks.text: Avoid paying large recruitment or placement fees without independently verifying the company, contract, and institute. A degree or training certificate does not guarantee a berth or a Third Officer appointment.

blocks.text: Promotion is not automatic. It depends on the required sea service, competency examinations, medical fitness, certificates, experience, and available positions. Progression to senior officer grades requires further certification and qualifying experience.

The Indian maritime administration's career guidance lists indicative monthly salary ranges for nautical officers, including approximately ₹1.2–2.0 lakh per month for a Third Officer. Actual pay varies by company, vessel type, flag, contract, experience, and employment terms.
Directorate General of Shipping

Treat these figures as a broad reference rather than a guaranteed starting salary. A deck cadet's pay is typically different from that of a licensed officer, and officers may be paid only during contracted periods onboard. Clarify whether the offer includes paid leave, insurance, travel, tax arrangements, and other benefits.
A Merchant Navy career differs substantially from a shore-based job. Before choosing this path, consider whether you are comfortable with:

items.text: Spending extended periods away from home and family.
Working rotating watches, including nights, weekends, and holidays.
Living and working in a confined environment with a multinational crew.
Following strict safety procedures and maintaining discipline under pressure.
Working in changing weather, ship motion, and potentially demanding operational conditions.
Managing fatigue, communication, and personal wellbeing during long contracts.

blocks.text: This career may suit someone who enjoys navigation, practical problem-solving, international exposure, teamwork, and structured responsibility. It may be less suitable for someone who needs a predictable daily schedule or regular access to home.

items.text: Electronic navigation and integrated bridge systems: increasingly connected navigation and monitoring systems.

blocks.label: E-navigation and digital voyage planning
blocks.text: improved exchange and use of navigational information.

items.text: Autonomous and remotely supported vessels: changing operational models, while qualified officers remain essential in many current shipboard roles.

blocks.label: Decarbonisation
blocks.text: alternative marine fuels, energy efficiency, and changing environmental requirements.

blocks.label: Cybersecurity
blocks.text: protecting navigation systems, ship networks, and operational technology.

blocks.label: Digital ship management
blocks.text: electronic records, predictive maintenance, and improved operational reporting.

A Third Officer should first master navigation, watchkeeping, safety, and maritime regulations. New technology is most useful when officers understand its limitations and know how to cross-check information.

A candidate preparing for the Third Officer pathway should ideally have:

items.text: An approved nautical science qualification.
Required maritime medical fitness and documentation.
Strong knowledge of navigation, collision regulations, and shipboard safety.
Completed approved training and qualifying sea service.

Good communication, situational awareness, teamwork, and professional discipline.

blocks.label: Follow the pathway carefully
blocks.text: eligibility and medical clearance → approved B.Sc. Nautical Science → deck-cadet sea service → required competency examinations and certification → Third Officer appointment.

Before committing to a college, verify the current requirements directly with the Indian Maritime University and the Directorate General of Maritime Administration. Their official resources provide the relevant admission, examination, and certification information.
IMU

The most important planning point is to secure a credible route to onboard training and qualifying sea service. Graduating from the degree programme is an important step, but it does not by itself qualify you to sail as a licensed Third Officer.
